newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic to accept opposition victory - sources.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic to accept opposition victory - sources.

text.p: Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic is expected on Saturday to acknowledge opposition victory at local elections and call for forming a coalition government, a senior political source said.
"Milosevic will endorse a report by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe in entirety. The statement is being written as we speak," the source told Reuters.

An OSCE mission led by former Spanish Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez last month endorsed all claims by the the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition. Zajedno claimed it won in 14 of Serbia's 18 largest cities including the capital Belgrade.

Milosevic's socialists annulled their victories, claiming unspecified irregularities. Cancellation of the November 17 election results triggered a wave of street protests, now in their eighth straight week, shaking the foundations of 52 years of leftist rule in Serbia.
The OSCE has given Belgrade authorities until January 16 to act on the recommendations by its mission.

The decision to uphold the OSCE report and call for a coalition government of "all left and democratic forces in the country for the sake of national interest" was made at a meeting on Friday by senior officials from the Socialist Party and the Yugoslav United Left, headed by Milosevic's hardliner wife Mirjana Markovic, the political source said.
